analysis:
The PR changes only XCTest files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/MiMo. It touches no production code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization, cache storage or the fan helper. No threat-model asset, trust boundary or mitigation changes.

In MiMoV26EncodedMediaIngressTests.swift (head lines ~343-347, 380) and MiMoV26ManagedAudioProviderTests.swift (patch hunks at ~242, ~271, ~301, ~343), the polling loop on managedMediaReservationCountForTesting is replaced. The new code installs a removal hook with setMediaReservationRemovalHookForTesting and waits on an EventCounter expectation. The tests still assert managedMediaReservationCountForTesting == 0 afterwards, so a leaked media reservation (an availability or resource-accounting concern under A-018 and TB-007) still fails the test. The change makes the tests deterministic and does not weaken the leak check.

The hook setter and EventCounter are test-only. The setter's definition was not supplied. It is presumably DEBUG or testing-gated, and the tests do not show whether it is compiled out of release builds. That is a minor unverified contract about the production side, not evidence of a regression.

One timing gap is minor. In the audio test the hook is installed before the request, and the expectation counts removals (reaching 1 or 2), so a settlement that arrives before the wait is not missed, provided the counter is cumulative.

The rest of the ingress test file is unchanged context. It already covers refusal of remote URIs, file URIs and oversized bodies, and rejection of unsupported controls before decode. It uses a synthetic bearer token and a fixture-only environment, with no real secrets.

The second patch excerpt is truncated, so the final lines of the audio test were not seen in full. The visible hunks are consistent with the change described. No findings.
